newsitem.title: MEXICO: Three main Pemex crude ports reopened - ports.
newsitem.headline: Three main Pemex crude ports reopened - ports.

text.p: Mexico's three main crude shipping ports were reopened Wednesday as winds died down along the Gulf of Mexico, port officials said.
Oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) confirmed that the ports had reopened.
The nation's most important crude shipping site, Cayo Arcas in Campeche state, reopened at noon (1800 GMT), port officials said.
Dos Bocas in Tabasco state reopened at 3 p.m. (2100 GMT) and Pajaritos in Veracruz state reopened at 1:15 p.m. (1915 GMT), port captains told Reuters.
Export shipments, which were suspended on Monday due to a polar front in the area, will be sent as soon as possible to clients, Pemex said.

Just two ports remain closed because of winds of about 50 mph (80 kph) have relaxed, the Communications and Transport ministry said in its meteorological bulletin. Ports still shut are Salina Cruz in Oaxaca state on the Pacific Coast and Frontera in Tabasco on the Gulf of Mexico.
